headline: Nikkei Asia reports that Taiwanese tech firms, led by TSMC with $265 billion of planned US investment, are rapidly building production abroad for the AI boom.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the TSMC figure dates from July and the report is a summary relayed second-hand.
importance_line: More AI server production moving to the US and Southeast Asia could shift where AI hardware is made, but much of it rests on plans and forecasts rather than finished plants.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports, as relayed by Seeking Alpha, that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, added $100 billion of spending in July, taking its planned US investment to $265 billion and its US sites to 12, while Quanta, Wistron and others have won approval to spend hundreds of millions of dollars on US server and circuit-board plants. A Taiwanese research institute projects that the US will hold 40% of Taiwanese firms' AI server capacity by 2030, up from 23% this year, with Taiwan's share falling from 47% to 30%.
notes: Read Seeking Alpha item on TradingView, which summarises Nikkei Asia; Nikkei original not opened. July $100B capex is background, not new. Projection is by Taiwan's Market Intelligence & Consulting Institute.
